question: Should OpenClaw core accept a bounded 512-row shared-SQLite `gateway_restart_audit` table that stores redacted restart source/session/preflight metadata for gateway restart forensics?
rationale: The code review did not find a concrete patch defect, but the PR creates a new durable local audit surface with operator/client metadata and touches restart availability paths; automation should not decide that privacy and retention policy for maintainers.

options.title: Accept Bounded Core Audit
options.body: Refresh the branch, rerun exact-head checks, and merge if maintainers accept the redacted 512-row local audit table as the core gateway restart forensic record.

options.title: Narrow Durable Payload
options.body: Ask the contributor to reduce persisted fields or move more details to non-durable logs before reconsidering the same core table shape.

options.title: Defer To Broader Audit Design
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers want gateway restart attribution to wait for a general audit-ledger design rather than a restart-specific table.

recommendation.title: Accept Bounded Core Audit
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch, rerun exact-head checks, and merge if maintainers accept the redacted 512-row local audit table as the core gateway restart forensic record.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal combines shared SQLite state, restart intent tracing, and database-first policy work adjacent to this PR's durable state boundary.
